(1) the concept ethnicity is used in HIV/STIs epidemiological research, but is not clearly defined or consistently operationalized; (2) the concept ethnicity in epidemiological research is constructed in a manner that is perpetually self-validifying; and (3) this construction is disseminated and operationalized through Dutch society, and so is perpetuated.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the construction of ethnicity as a category of health disparities in HIV/STIs in the Netherlands is perpetuated and how it is related to the construction of ethnic minorities as a high-risk problem group.
the construction and operationalisation of the concept ethnicity, as well as its implications for the social construction and representation of ethnic minority populations in the Netherlands.
how the concept of ethnicity is constructed, and what this construction means in the context of HIV and STI surveillance, prevention and treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RIVM's construction of ethnicity is a social construct that is self-fulfilling and self-validating.

ethnicity is a social construct that is used to describe the health status and sexual practices of ethnic minority groups, in a self-fulfilling manner, in order to justify the allocation of resources to ethnic groups.
the RIVM has created a self-fulfilling ethnic construction that has been disseminated throughout society and is now a part of Dutch social and public health policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ethnicity as a category of difference is a powerful and pervasive concept that is constructed and re-constructed in the HIV/STI field in the Netherlands.
the construction of the high risk sexual other is a result of the interaction between the RIVM and Dutch society.
, the RIVM's epidemiological research on HIV/STIs in The Netherlands has led to the creation of an ethnic construct that is perpetually self-validizing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the concept of ethnicity is a social construction that has a material impact on the lives of ethnic minorities and that this impact can be traced through the social, political and scientific processes that produce the construct.

the construction of ethnic minorities as a high-risk sexual problem group is a social and scientific process that is self-validating and self-reinforcing, and so the ethnic minority problem group becomes a social fact.

the construction of the ethnic other as high risk for HIV/STIs is a powerful social and scientific construct that is perpetuated through a complex and dynamic interaction between epidemiological research, media and political rhetoric and prevention practice.
